speaker: Mr David Hoe
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) what does the targeted and stepped-up surveillance entail in practice for central kitchens under SFA's risk-based food safety inspection regime; and (b) whether SFA will consider classifying central kitchens supplying school meals as a distinct higher-risk tier and subjecting them to sustained stepped-up surveillance, in view of large volumes served to children and heightened consequences and disruptions from any lapse.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This is consistently applied to central kitchens and caterers serving all consumers, including other vulnerable consumers such as persons in nursing homes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: In addition, central kitchens are graded under the Safety Assurance for Food Establishment (SAFE) framework.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: In the event of a major food safety lapse, they will be downgraded upon completion of suspension or Court conviction and inspected more regularly.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The up-to-date representation of the establishment’s food safety performance via its SAFE grade allows service buyers and consumers to have a peace of mind to make more informed decisions on the food establishment to procure from.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Against this backdrop, I have four supplementary questions.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: What kind of assurance does SFA give on compliance and safety for ingredient suppliers to our central kitchens?

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Because they prepare and they distribute quite a significant amount of food.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: On the second topic – which would be about our target population, which is our children – beyond frequent inspection would the Ministry consider placing more safeguards on central kitchens, given the vulnerable young children and also the impact if such lapses were to occur again?

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: What assurance mechanism would there be for schools to be confident that the central kitchen operators are fully compliant with SFA requirements, not only just at appointment, but on an ongoing basis?

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Lastly, before food distribution, what kind of requirements and checks must be met before it is being sent out?

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: And in light of the recent incident, would SFA consider tightening the requirements before food can be sent out?

speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
text: The first one was about assurance around ingredient suppliers in central kitchens.

speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
text: SFA also, of course, inspects central kitchens to ensure food handling is done properly and there is proper segregation between raw ingredients and food products.

speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
text: That is for the first supplementary question from the Member.

speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
text: The second one was about what we can do beyond more frequent inspections.

speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
text: As I covered in my main reply, beyond more frequent inspections, and this is largely due to the larger scale of food preparation and processing that caterers and central kitchens do, additional inspections are also done on these central kitchens if they are found to have repeated food safety lapses.

speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
text: So, there is an additional step-up in terms of frequency of inspections.

speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
text: I think it is also important to then note that these gastroenteritis outbreaks are due to more than one factor usually.

speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
text: And this is not just from issues that arise from the central kitchens but also could be due to onsite handling and preparation issues or it could be due to handling during the transportation process by the transport service provider.

speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
text: So, it requires then SFA to work with all the relevant stakeholders to ensure that our food management system addresses all points of this process.

speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
text: The third part, in terms of operator selection, the Member asked on assurance mechanisms.

speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
text: As part of licensing conditions, the central kitchens do have to implement food safety measures and of course, as the regulator, SFA then conducts inspections to ensure compliance.

speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
text: At the same time, there were some Parliamentary Questions filed on the SAFE framework that was just launched.

speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
text: This is a shift from the annual snapshot assessments that the previous grading system was based on.

speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
text: And lastly, there was also a question around pre-distribution requirements for central kitchens to adhere to.

speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
text: There are a couple of requirements under SFA's licensing requirements.

speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
text: This ensures that there is no cross contamination.

speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
text: We also require them to identify what we call critical control points along the food preparation process and this helps to monitor potential risks in critical junctures of the food handling process within the central kitchens.

speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
text: And finally, we also then require appointment of a food hygiene officer to oversee the implementation of these measures.

speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
text: So, holistically this helps to hopefully ensure that there is some level of standards before these foods are distributed out of the central kitchens.
